description: Search the Australian Food Composition Database (AFCD Release 3.0, Food Standards Australia New Zealand) for foods by name (GET https://www.foodstandards.gov.au/science-data/food-nutrient-databases/afcd/search/api/foods/alphabetical, the complete catalogue of 1,588 foods, or /foods/alphabetical/{letter} when `letter` is given). AFCD has no server-side search: the program applies `query` as a case-insensitive substring match over the food name and its `inclusions` (alternative names), exactly as the AFCD site does, then filters by food group / sub food group and pages the result. Each row carries the Public Food Key (pfk) for get_food, the AUSNUT classification code, the food group pair and the public food page URL. Returns an empty `foods` list for a query nothing matches; `not_found` for a food_group_id / sub_food_group_id that does not exist in AFCD or a page past the last one.

description: Predicted protein complexes in AlphaFold DB that contain a protein, by UniProt accession, entry name, model ID, entry URL or gene symbol and organism; or one complex by its model ID (AF-0000000065932364). Each complex lists its partners (UniProt accession, gene, protein name, organism, copies), assembly, the provider dataset (mostly NVIDIA's proteome-scale homo- and heterodimers), mean pLDDT, the interface scores ipTM, ipSAE, pDockQ, pDockQ2 and LIS, interface_confidence from ipTM (high 0.8 or more, medium 0.6 to 0.8, low under 0.6), links to the mmCIF and PAE image, and its entry page. Sorted by ipTM, highest first; min_iptm filters and limit caps the list. A protein with no predicted complexes returns an empty list.

description: The AlphaFold DB predicted structure of one protein, by UniProt accession (P04637), isoform (P04637-2), entry name (P53_HUMAN), AlphaFold model ID (AF-P04637-F1, AF-0000000000710001), alphafold.ebi.ac.uk entry URL, or gene symbol and organism. Returns the model ID, version, date, method and provider, the UniProt residue range it covers, mean pLDDT and the share of residues per confidence band with a one-line reading, confident_regions (pLDDT 70 or more) and disordered_regions (pLDDT under 50) as UniProt residue ranges, whether AlphaMissense data exists, and links to the mmCIF, BinaryCIF, PDB, PAE and per-residue confidence files (coordinates are linked, never returned). Isoform and alternative models of the entry are listed in other_models. Merged UniProt accessions are followed. Unknown or deleted accessions and proteins AlphaFold DB does not model (it covers 16 to 2,700 residues) are not_found with the reason.

description: AlphaMissense pathogenicity predictions (Google DeepMind) for a human protein, from AlphaFold DB: every possible amino-acid substitution scored 0 to 1 and classed likely benign (under 0.34), ambiguous, or likely pathogenic (over 0.564). Pass variants (R175H, p.Arg175His; up to 50) for their scores and classes, checked against the UniProt canonical sequence. Every call also returns a protein summary: class fractions, mean score and sensitive_regions, the residue ranges whose mean score is above 0.564. Takes the same identifiers as prediction. Canonical human sequences only: other organisms and isoforms are not_found. These are research predictions, not clinical classifications.

description: Full current OCI price list in one currency, one record per part x price tier, paged in memory: every page re-fetches `GET /products/?currencyCode=<currency>` (no server pagination exists; `offset` and `limit` are ignored by the API) and returns the next `page_size` parts. The cursor pins the currency, `lastUpdated` and the SHA-256 of the canonical items; a page that finds either changed fails with `invalid_input` code `publication_changed` instead of mixing versions. Segment key: `currency`. Collection contract name: `records/list`.

description: Cheap version check of the OCI price list: one `GET /products/?currencyCode=<currency>` (about 200 KB for USD). Returns `lastUpdated` as `publication_id` and `published_at`, the part count, the tier (record) count, the response size and the SHA-256 of the canonical items. Oracle posts no hash of its own and sends an ETag that differs per query and is not honoured by `If-None-Match`, so it is not used. No delta endpoint exists, so `records/changes` is not offered. Collection contract name: `source/status`.

description: Search the Arizona ROC contractor register (Aura action ARCP_ContractorSearch.getRecords, the site's 'Contractor Search'). `query` matches a business name, a person's name ('First Last'), or a ROC license number (6 digits, with or without the 'ROC ' prefix); `classifications` filters by license classification exactly as `list_classifications` spells them (e.g. 'C-42 Roofing'; the site matches the classification family loosely, a 'C-42 Roofing' filter also returns 'CR-42 Roofing' licenses); `city` filters by the licensee's Arizona city. At least one criterion is required. Results are grouped the way the site shows them: one row per business/account with its contacts (name and role) and every license it holds (license_id, ROC license number, status such as Active / Suspended / Revoked / Expired, classification, qualifying party or QP-exempt). The server returns the whole result set in one answer (a broad single-word query can be several hundred accounts and take a few seconds); this function pages through it client-side with `page_size` rows per page and an offset `cursor`, re-running the same search for each page. A search that matches nothing is a valid empty result (`accounts: []`).

description: The full current list (the batch's `records/list`), paginated with a cursor pinned to one publication. Every page re-reads the file's trailer, recomputes the publication id and compares it with the one in the cursor; when the source moved on the call fails with invalid_input whose issue code is `publication_changed` (message prefixed `publication_changed:`), never mixing publications. Pages are read as Range segments of the 34 MB consolidated.json from the pinned byte offset; on resume the last record of the previous page is re-read and its `SOURCE:id` checked against the cursor, so a re-ordered file is also reported as publication_changed. Filters: `sources` (list abbreviations; ISN is accepted for ACN), `exclude_treasury` (drops SDN, SSI, FSE, CAP, CMIC, MBS, PLC, which `sanctionssearch-ofac-treas-gov` already covers), `entity_types`, `programs` (exact program strings). A page reads until `limit` records matched or the file ended (the whole 34 MB file scans in under 10 s), so a filtered page shorter than `limit` normally means the list is exhausted; `next_cursor` is null exactly when it is. Records are grouped by source in the file (ACN first, SDN the bulk, UVL last on 2026-10-17) but no order is promised.

Records are grouped by source in the file (ACN first, SDN the bulk, UVL last on 2026-10-17) but no order is promised.

description: Version check of the current consolidated.json (the batch's `source/status`; named with an underscore because function names must be identifiers). One Range request for the file's trailer returns the publication id (SHA-256 over the sorted `source=source_last_updated` lines of `sources_used` plus the record total: it moves only when an agency publishes or the count changes, unlike the ETag, Last-Modified and `search_performed_at`, which change at every hourly rebuild), the build time, the per-source import state, the record count, the JSON/CSV/TSV file URLs and the JSON size. The publisher posts no hash; with `content_hash: true` the function walks the whole file in Range segments (about 34 MB, 30-90 s) and returns the SHA-256 of the sorted per-record canonical SHA-256 digests, an order-independent hash of the records themselves.

description: Text-mined annotations of one article from the Europe PMC annotations platform (SciLite): the genes and proteins, diseases, chemicals, organisms, GO terms, experimental methods and database accession numbers named in it, each grounded to a database identifier (UniProt, NCBI Taxonomy, ChEBI, GO, UMLS, EFO, PDB, ENA and others), plus gene-disease, gene-drug and disease-drug relationships (Open Targets) and gene-function statements (SIB). Entities are merged per identifier with a mention count, the matched spellings, the sections they occur in and one example in context, sorted by mentions; relationships keep the sentence that states them. Coverage is the abstract for every article and the body for open-access full text. For an article whose licence does not allow commercial reuse, sentences and context from outside the title and abstract are left out (`text_withheld`) while entities and identifiers stay. Europe PMC publishes annotations as public domain.

Text is returned only when Europe PMC lists the article as open access under CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA or CC BY-ND and the article's own licence statement agrees; otherwise `availability` is `license_restricted` (CC BY-NC variants, free-to-read only) or `not_available` (no open full text) with a message and the europepmc.org link, and no text. description: The complete Canadian Nutrient File record of one food by `food_code` (or a pasted CNF serving-portion / nutrientReport page URL): description, every nutrient the CNF reports for it per 100 g edible portion, joined with the CNF nutrient dictionary (symbol, INFOODS tagname, unit such as g / mg / µg / IU / kcal, decimals, nutrient group) and the data-source code list (provenance; source 1 marks values changed to meet Canadian fortification regulations), plus the food's serving measures with conversion factors and gram weights, refuse (inedible portion) rows and yield rows. Nutrients the CNF does not report for a food are absent, never zero-filled. `nutrient_ids` restricts the nutrient rows (203 Protein, 208 Energy kcal, 301 Calcium, 339 Vitamin D µg, 324 Vitamin D IU, ...; see `list_nutrients`); `measure` names one of the food's measures (e.g. '250ml') and adds `value_per_measure` to every nutrient row. Seven to eight anonymous GET calls to /api/canadian-nutrient-file/ (food, nutrientamount, servingsize, refuseamount, yieldamount, nutrientname, nutrientgroup, nutrientsource). An unknown food code is `not_found` (the API answers an empty list).

description: One page (100 rows) of the full GDACS event list for one segment: hazard types x calendar date window, from events/geteventlist/SEARCH with alertlevel=green;orange;red always sent (the API default silently hides Green). Rows are episodes ordered by todate descending; every record carries source_record_id gdacs:<eventtype>:<eventid>:<episodeid>, source_url, publication_id and retrieved_at. publication_id = segment + the newest datemodified on page 1. A window that ended more than 30 days ago is closed: later pages re-fetch page 1 and return invalid_input with issue code publication_changed when the pin moved. A window ending within 30 days of today is live (live: true, coverage partial): rows may shift between pages, so dedupe on source_record_id and reconcile with records_changes. Default segment: the current calendar month to today. Events overlapping the window (long droughts, cyclones) are included even when they started earlier.

A window ending within 30 days of today is live (live: true, coverage partial): rows may shift between pages, so dedupe on source_record_id and reconcile with records_changes. Default segment: the current calendar month to today. Events overlapping the window (long droughts, cyclones) are included even when they started earlier.

description: Cheap version check of the USA Structures publication. Reads the hub downloads page (portal item data) for the current state zip link of every state and territory (56 rows; the bucket listing omits current files, so the page is authoritative), HEADs each zip on the public S3 bucket for size, ETag (multipart MD5, the publisher's only posted hash), x-amz-version-id and Last-Modified, derives the release date from the file name (PR_Structures_20260913 -> 2026-09-13; Deliverable20250606TX -> 2025-06-06), and reports the hosted view's dataLastEditDate as the records publication id. With `state` set, adds the view's row count for that state; with `include_fgdc` (one state only) two or three S3 range reads parse the zip central directory and the embedded FGDC metadata XML (publication date, imagery date range, access and use constraints). Every state file exceeds the 32 MiB fetch cap (only the small territories AS, GU, MP, VI and DC fit), so `handoff` is true for them: download the file_url out of band and use records_list for rows.

description: Full current list of IBM Cloud list prices, one record per plan x deployment (region) x metric x country x quantity tier, walked in catalog order: `GET /api/v1?q=kind:<kind>&_limit=200&_offset=N` (service, iaas, platform_service, composite by default), then `GET /api/v1/{entry}/plan`, then for each plan tagged `paid` `GET /api/v1/{plan}/pricing/deployment` (all pages of 50). The cursor pins the listing ETag and the newest pricing `effective_from` seen; a page that finds a different ETag or a newer `effective_from` fails with `invalid_input` code `publication_changed` instead of mixing versions. Segment key: `entry_id` restricts the walk to one catalog entry. Each page prices at most `plans_per_page` plans and examines at most 20 entries. VPC plans are joined to their `*.profile` entry (vCPU, memory, tenancy). Filters (`regions`, `countries`, `metrics`, `plans_per_page`) are not stored in the cursor: pass them again with `continuation`. Collection contract name: `records/list`.

description: Every HTS line of the current revision, segmented by chapter: `exportList?from=CC00&to=CC99&format=JSON&styles=false` for one two-digit chapter per segment, paged by `limit` rows. Before each page the current revision name is re-read (`reststop/currentRelease`) and compared with the one pinned in the cursor; if it moved the call fails with `invalid_input` and issue code `publication_changed` on `/continuation` instead of mixing revisions (the server always serves the current revision; it ignores `release=`). Chapter 77 is reserved and empty; empty chapters are skipped. Rows are mapped per the collection contract: `htsno` as `source_record_id` (unnumbered headings get `<chapter>:<ordinal>` and a `parent_htsno`), derived `hts_level`, `hs6`, `statistical_suffix`, `chapter`. Collection contract name: `records/list`.

description: Search the JLCPCB parts library. Accepts a free-text keyword (description words, an LCSC C-number such as C5358, or a manufacturer part number such as STM32F103C8T6) and/or a category, with optional manufacturer, package, availability tab, basic/extended and sort filters. Returns one page of parts with stock, assembly and purchase price breaks (USD), package, type, attributes, datasheet and canonical URLs. description: Search the Florida DBPR licensee registry (POST /portalsearches/VerifyLicensee/Results). Two modes: by license number (`license_number`, SearchType=SearchByLicenseNumber) or by name (`last_name` / `first_name` / `middle_name` for individuals, `org_name` for businesses and establishments; SearchType=SearchByName). Name searches accept the site's optional filters: `board` (2-3 digit DBPR board code, e.g. 06 Construction Industry, 25 Real Estate), `license_type` (4-digit code within the board), `county` (Florida county code, e.g. 39 Hillsborough, 47 Leon, 23 Dade), `city` and `state`, and `include_historic` for licenses no longer current. Returns the results table as displayed: one row per licensee name (a licensee with a DBA appears once as `Primary` and once as `DBA`, both with the same detail_id), with license type, license number and rank, status and expiry, the address block and the 32-hex detail_id that `get_license_detail`, `get_license_relations` and `get_license_complaints` take. `per_page` rows per page (default 10); the continuation cursor is `<page>:<total_records>` because the site needs the total echoed back to page. A search with no match is a valid empty result (the site's 'There were no records found' message with 'Search Results - 0 Records'), not an error. `data_as_of` is the site's nightly refresh stamp.

Name searches accept the site's optional filters: `board` (2-3 digit DBPR board code, e.g. 06 Construction Industry, 25 Real Estate), `license_type` (4-digit code within the board), `county` (Florida county code, e.g. 39 Hillsborough, 47 Leon, 23 Dade), `city` and `state`, and `include_historic` for licenses no longer current. Returns the results table as displayed: one row per licensee name (a licensee with a DBA appears once as `Primary` and once as `DBA`, both with the same detail_id), with license type, license number and rank, status and expiry, the address block and the 32-hex detail_id that `get_license_detail`, `get_license_relations` and `get_license_complaints` take. `per_page` rows per page (default 10); the continuation cursor is `<page>:<total_records>` because the site needs the total echoed back to page. A search with no match is a valid empty result (the site's 'There were no records found' message with 'Search Results - 0 Records'), not an error. `data_as_of` is the site's nightly refresh stamp.

description: One page of rows from one bulk file (ep-3), segment key (type, year). Each page re-fetches the gzip, stream-decompresses it through an RFC 4180 parser (narratives hold commas, quotes and newlines), skips to the row offset, returns up to 2000 typed rows and stops. The cursor pins file name and ETag; if NCEI reissued the file in between (new c date, missing old name or different ETag) the call fails with upstream_error `publication_changed: ...` instead of mixing versions. Every row carries source_record_id, source_url, publication_id and retrieved_at; DAMAGE_* are kept verbatim with a parsed USD value beside them.

description: Search human genes in the Human Protein Atlas by subcellular location (one of HPA's 49 terms, with a minimum reliability and optionally main locations only), by RNA tissue or single cell type specificity (enriched, group enriched or enhanced in a named tissue or cell type), by free text or HPA search syntax, or any combination (ANDed). A location search ranks by that location's own reliability, then main before additional; a tissue or cell type search ranks by specificity, then expression there; a text search keeps HPA's order. Each result has the gene, Ensembl and UniProt IDs, the matched location with its reliability and GO ID, all main and additional locations, and the requested RNA specificity. HPA returns whole result sets, so total_count is exact and next_offset pages on. An empty result is a valid empty page; an unknown tissue or cell type name is invalid_input.

description: Full text of a PubMed Central article from the NCBI BioC RESTful service (ep-31, `pmcoa.cgi`), which serves the PMC Open Access subset: title, license, article ids, authors, year and every passage (abstract, section headings, paragraphs, table and figure captions) with its section type, in reading order. `availability` is `full_text` when body passages are present, `abstract_only` when the OA record has only front matter (typical for preprints), and `not_in_open_access_subset` when PMC knows the article but does not license its text for the service (then `sections` is empty and ids come from the PMC ID Converter, ep-25). Accepts a PMCID or a `pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC.../` URL; an unknown PMCID is `not_found`. `max_chars` truncates the concatenated text.

description: The full current list of SAM.gov exclusions from the daily public extract (SAM_Exclusions_Public_Extract_V2_YYDDD.ZIP: about 169,000 rows, individuals, firms, special entity designations and vessels), paged with a cursor pinned to the file name and its S3 ETag. Optional classification filter. Each daily file is a full snapshot: there is no exclusions changes feed, diff consecutive snapshots.

description: Find OECD dataflows by keyword: id, agency, version, name and the `dataflow_ref` every other function takes, from GET dataflow/{agency}/all/latest?detail=allstubs (about 1,500 public dataflows with `agency` = all). `q` filters by a case-insensitive substring of the name or id (e.g. `revenue statistics`, `social expenditure`, `sector accounts`, `merchandise trade`). Common dataflows: G20/OECD merchandise trade OECD.SDD.TPS:DSD_IMTS@DF_IMTS (REF_AREA incl. G20, G7, OECD; TRADE_FLOW X exports, M imports, TB balance; FREQ Q/M/A; UNIT_MEASURE USD_EXC); quarterly trade in services and goods from balance of payments OECD.SDD.TPS:DSD_BOP@DF_BOP (MEASURE S services, G goods; ACCOUNTING_ENTRY C credit (exports), D debit (imports), B balance; FREQ Q); annual services by partner and category OECD.SDD.TPS:DSD_BOP@DF_TIS; Revenue Statistics OECD.CTP.TPS:DSD_REV_COMP_OECD@DF_RSOECD (STANDARD_REVENUE _T total tax, T_1000 income, T_1100 personal income, T_1200 corporate, T_2000 social security, T_4000 property, T_5000 goods and services; UNIT_MEASURE PT_B1GQ % of GDP; SECTOR S13 general government); Social expenditure (SOCX) OECD.ELS.SPD:DSD_SOCX_AGG@DF_SOCX_AGG (EXPEND_SOURCE ES10 public, ES20 mandatory private; PROGRAMME_TYPE _T total, TP11 old age...; UNIT_MEASURE PT_B1GQ % of GDP); quarterly sector accounts OECD.SDD.NAD:DSD_NASEC1@DF_QSA (SECTOR S1 total economy, S11 non-financial corporations, S13 government, S14 households, S1M households and NPISH; TRANSACTION B6G disposable income, B8G saving, B9 net lending...); annual sector accounts OECD.SDD.NAD:DSD_NASEC10@DF_TABLE14. Countries are ISO3 codes in REF_AREA; periods are 2024, 2024-Q3, 2024-07.

description: Search hourly/daily (transient) parking around a coordinate for an arrival/departure window (api.spothero.com/v2/search/transient, the request behind spothero.com/search). Each result is a facility with its address, distance from the origin, rating, live availability, access hours, restrictions, vehicle limits and one or more priced quotes for the window: `total_price` (what SpotHero charges, service fee included) and `advertised_price` (the headline rate without the fee), itemised. Event rates can widen the priced window; read each quote's `starts`/`ends`. Pass a SpotHero `destination_id` to anchor the search on a venue (its coordinates from `destination`) and to get `spot_url` links. Pages via `cursor`/`next_cursor`. Prices are USD in the US and CAD in Canada, taxes not itemised.

description: Values of one or more series of a Statistics Canada table, chosen by member names instead of raw coordinates. members maps a dimension (its English or French name, or its position) to one member or a list of members (name, unique part of a name, or member_id); every combination is fetched, up to 50 series. Dimensions left out use their first member (usually Canada or the total). A table-viewer URL's pickMembers selection is honoured when members is omitted; coordinates (e.g. 2.2.0.0.0.0.0.0.0.0) are accepted instead. Returns the latest_n periods (default 12) or a start_period/end_period range per series, each with its vector id, title, unit, scale, decimals, member names and data points (reference period, value, preliminary/revised symbol, status and confidentiality flags, release time). Series the table does not hold are listed in missing; when none exist the call is not_found. Requests over 20,000 data points are refused; narrow the range. WDS getCubeMetadata, getSeriesInfoFromCubePidCoord and getDataFromVectorsAndLatestNPeriods / getDataFromVectorByReferencePeriodRange; full-table CSV downloads are never fetched.

description: Describe one Statistics Canada table: title, frequency, coverage dates, last release, archive status, series and data-point counts, and every dimension with its members (member_id, parent, English and French names, geographic classification code, unit). This is how to find the member names or ids table_data takes (e.g. Geography = Edmonton, Alberta; Products and product groups = All-items). member_query keeps only members whose name contains the text (case and accents ignored), and max_members caps each dimension's list (members_truncated says when). Footnotes are counted and returned with include_footnotes. WDS getCubeMetadata plus getCodeSets for unit names. An unknown table id is not_found.

description: One page of the full consolidated list (XML 1.1), in file order (ascending logicalId), optionally filtered by programme code (UKR, IRN, SYR, ... 34 codes in the current file) and entity type (person, organization). The cursor is pinned to the publication (the file's SHA-1): every page re-reads the feed and the file, and when the publication has moved on the call fails with invalid_input, issue code `publication_changed`, instead of mixing two versions; restart without a cursor. Each record carries source_record_id (eu:<logicalId>), entity_type, primary_name, names (all languages and scripts), identifiers, addresses, nationalities, birth_dates (partial and approximate kept as given), birth_places, programs, measures (always asset_freeze), legal_basis, listed_on (designationDate, or the earliest amendment date when the file omits it), un_reference, remarks, and the provenance fields source_url, publication_id, retrieved_at. `total` counts the entities matching the filter in the whole file; `publication.record_count` is the file's entity count. Every page costs one feed request and one gzip-compressed download of the 25 MB file (about 2.5 MB on the wire), so prefer large pages (up to 500).
